dumaguete.title: Dumaguete Travel Guides: Food, Budget and Day Trips
dumaguete.description: Dumaguete travel guides: getting there from Cebu, a 3-day budget, breakfast spots, a first food trip, the Buglasan Festival and day trips from the city.
dumaguete.keywords: Dumaguete travel guides, things to do in Dumaguete, Dumaguete budget trip, Dumaguete food, Cebu to Dumaguete, Siquijor from Dumaguete, Buglasan Festival
intro: Dumaguete is the capital of Negros Oriental, a small, walkable city on the southeastern coast of Negros Island. It is a university town first: Silliman University, founded in 1901, sits right in the middle of it, and the students shape the cafes, the cheap eats and the slow pace of the place. The seafront Rizal Boulevard is where the city goes in the early morning and again at sunset.

Most people come for a mix of city time and day trips, and Dumaguete works well as a base for both. Within an hour or two you can reach Apo Island for snorkelling, the Twin Lakes in the hills of Sibulan, dolphin watching and the Manjuyod sandbar off Bais, or the ferry to Siquijor. Getting here is straightforward: the airport is in neighbouring Sibulan, and ferries and fast craft link the port with Cebu, Siquijor and Bohol. The sea or road guide compares the routes.

It is also one of the more affordable cities in the Visayas. A three-day trip on a budget is realistic, and food is a big part of the appeal, from breakfast spots to a first-timer's food trip. October is the busiest month for local events, with the Buglasan Festival bringing the towns of the province into the city.

The stories below cover the city itself, how it is changing, and its festivals and events. Ferry times, fares and event schedules change from season to season, so confirm them before you travel. Still choosing between this city and Cebu? Read Dumaguete vs Cebu first, and see the Negros Oriental guides for the rest of the province.

negros-oriental.title: Negros Oriental Travel Guides: Beyond Dumaguete
negros-oriental.description: Negros Oriental travel guides beyond Dumaguete: weekend trips for every budget, Mabinay caves, Bais dolphin watching, mountain cafes and beach resorts.
negros-oriental.keywords: Negros Oriental travel guides, things to do in Negros Oriental, Negros Oriental weekend getaways, Mabinay, Bais dolphin watching, Pamplona cafe, La Libertad beach resort
intro: Negros Oriental covers the eastern half of Negros Island, a long strip of coast backed by mountains and volcanic highlands. Dumaguete is the capital and the easiest base, but most of what makes the province worth the trip is outside the city: towns where the main road still passes rice fields and small markets, and a coastline with far fewer resorts than Cebu or Bohol.

Head north and you reach Bais, known for dolphin watching and the Manjuyod sandbar, and Tanjay, with views from the hills above town. Inland, Mabinay has dozens of caves, and Pamplona and San Jose have farm cafes in the cooler uplands. Head south and the coast runs past Zamboanguita, the jumping-off point for Apo Island, toward Siaton and the beaches beyond. Along the northern coast are quiet beach towns such as La Libertad, and inland, Canlaon City sits on the slopes of Kanlaon Volcano, so check the current alert level before planning anything on that side.

Public transport is mostly buses and vans along the coastal highway, with tricycles and habal-habal for the last stretch. That works for the main towns, but caves, waterfalls and mountain cafes are easier with a hired car or driver, especially in the rainy months when side roads turn muddy. The weekend getaways for different budgets and places worth the drive are good places to start.

The stories below follow the province beyond the city limits, newest first. Distances look short on a map, but mountain roads are slow, and opening hours at smaller attractions change, so confirm before you set out. For food, budgets and events in the city itself, see the Dumaguete guides.

cebu.title: Cebu Travel Guides: Itineraries, Day Trips and Festivals
cebu.description: Cebu travel guides: a 3-day itinerary, Oslob and Kawasan Falls, Bantayan and Malapascua, Sinulog, heritage walks and local food, with notes on costs.
cebu.keywords: Cebu travel guides, Cebu itinerary, things to do in Cebu, Cebu day trips, Sinulog Cebu, Oslob whale shark, Kawasan Falls canyoneering, Bantayan Island, Malapascua
intro: Cebu is a long, narrow island in the middle of the Visayas, and most trips start at Mactan-Cebu International Airport or the ports of Cebu City. The city is the busy part: old streets, churches and Carbon Market downtown, malls and hotels uptown, and the hills of Busay just above it. The three-day itinerary is a good first plan, and the heritage walk covers the old quarter on foot.

Leave the city and the island splits into two very different trips. The south is for the classic day trips: Oslob for whale sharks and Sumilon Island, Moalboal for the sardine run, Badian for canyoneering at Kawasan Falls, and Dalaguete for the climb up Osmeña Peak. Plan on long bus rides from the South Bus Terminal, and start early, because the road along the coast is slow after mid-morning. The north is quieter and better for staying a few nights: Bantayan Island for flat white-sand beaches, Malapascua for diving with thresher sharks, and the Camotes Islands to the east for lakes, caves and empty coves.

Timing matters more than most visitors expect. The driest months are usually from about January to May, while the second half of the year brings more rain and the chance of typhoons, which can cancel boats at short notice. January is also Sinulog month, when Cebu City fills up and hotel prices rise. The month-by-month guide goes through what each part of the year is like.

The guides below are newest first, with the most useful starting points at the top. Fees, boat schedules and rules at places like Oslob change, so check the current details with the operator or the town tourism office before you go. Crossing to Negros? The Dumaguete and Negros Oriental pages pick up where this one ends, and the Visayas guides cover Bohol, Siquijor and the islands farther out.

luzon.title: Luzon Travel Guides: Mountains, Beaches and Food
luzon.description: Luzon travel guides: Baguio, Sagada, Banaue, Vigan, Batanes, Manila food crawls, La Union and Baler surf, Zambales coves, Mayon and Bicol, with costs.
luzon.keywords: Luzon travel guides, things to do in Luzon, Baguio, Sagada, Banaue rice terraces, Vigan, Batanes, Manila food trip, La Union surfing, Zambales coves, Mayon Volcano
intro: Luzon is the largest island in the Philippines and the one with the most variety in a single trip. In the north are the cool mountain towns of the Cordillera, the old Spanish-era streets of Ilocos and the far-off islands of Batanes. Manila sits in the middle, and the long tail of the island runs south through Batangas and down to the volcanoes and islands of Bicol.

The mountains are the main draw for many visitors. Baguio is the easiest to reach, and it gets crowded during Panagbenga in February and on long weekends. Farther in, Sagada has caves and hanging coffins, the rice terraces of Banaue and Batad are a full day by road, and Mount Pulag is known for its sea of clouds at dawn. Expect long, winding drives and cold nights, and pack layers even in summer.

Closer to Manila, the trips get shorter. Zambales has camping coves and the Mount Pinatubo crater lake, Pampanga is a food trip built around sisig, and La Union and Baler are the surf towns. To the south, Tagaytay overlooks Taal Lake, Anilao is a dive spot within driving distance of the capital, and Bicol has Mayon Volcano, the Caramoan islands and the whale sharks of Donsol. In Manila itself, the guides cover a 24-hour stopover in Intramuros and a food crawl through Binondo.

Distances on Luzon are big, so most people pick one region per trip rather than trying to see it all. The northern half catches most of the typhoons between about June and November, and mountain roads can close after heavy rain, so leave a spare day. Fees, permits and transport schedules change, so check current details with the local tourism office before you go.

palawan-mimaropa.title: Palawan and MIMAROPA Travel Guides: Coron, Mindoro, Romblon
palawan-mimaropa.description: Palawan and MIMAROPA travel guides: Coron wrecks, Underground River permits, quiet Palawan beaches, Puerto Galera, Romblon and the Moriones Festival.
palawan-mimaropa.keywords: Palawan travel guides, MIMAROPA, Coron, El Nido, Puerto Princesa Underground River, Puerto Galera, Romblon, Sibuyan Island, Marinduque Moriones Festival
intro: MIMAROPA takes its name from the provinces it groups together: Mindoro (split into Occidental and Oriental), Marinduque, Romblon and Palawan. On official maps it belongs to Luzon, but none of it is on the main island, so every trip here starts with a flight or a boat, and each province works as a separate destination rather than one long route.

Palawan draws most of the visitors, and the first decision is which part of it to base yourself in. The El Nido, Coron and Puerto Princesa comparison lays out how they differ in cost, travel time and pace. Coron suits divers and island-hoppers, with Second World War wrecks in the bay, while Puerto Princesa is the base for the Underground River, a UNESCO World Heritage Site where visitor numbers are capped, so read the permit guide before booking flights.

The rest of the region is quieter and slower to reach. Puerto Galera on Mindoro is the easiest escape from Manila, a short boat ride from Batangas, with beaches and dive sites close together. Romblon has marble workshops, old forts and the hard climb up Mount Guiting-Guiting on Sibuyan. Marinduque comes alive in Holy Week, when masked Moriones fill the streets of Boac and nearby towns; the Moriones guide has the dates and the best days to go.

Island-hopping trips and ferries here depend on the sea, and boats stay in port whenever the coast guard raises a warning, so leave a spare day before any flight out. Environmental fees, permit rules and tour prices change from season to season, and each town sets its own, so confirm them with the local tourism office or your operator before you travel.

visayas.title: Visayas Travel Guides: Bohol, Siquijor, Iloilo and More
visayas.description: Visayas travel guides beyond Cebu and Negros Oriental: Bohol, Siquijor, Bacolod and Silay, Iloilo and Guimaras, Boracay, Leyte and Samar, with real costs.
visayas.keywords: Visayas travel guides, Bohol, Panglao, Siquijor, Bacolod, Silay, Iloilo, Guimaras, Boracay, Antique, Leyte, Samar, Biliran, Kalanggaman Island
intro: The Visayas are the islands in the middle of the Philippines, grouped today into four regions: Western Visayas, the Negros Island Region, Central Visayas and Eastern Visayas. Cebu, Dumaguete and Negros Oriental each have their own page on this site, so this one gathers everything else, from islands an hour's boat ride from Cebu to provinces most visitors never reach.

Bohol and Siquijor are the easiest additions to a Cebu or Dumaguete trip. Bohol has the beaches of Panglao and Alona Beach, the tarsiers of Corella and quieter coves in the east around Anda. Siquijor is small enough to circle in a day by motorbike, but it rewards a slower pace, and the three-day ring road plan spreads the falls, beaches and old churches over a few days.

To the west, Negros Occidental pairs Bacolod's food and its October MassKara Festival with the heritage houses of Silay. Across the Guimaras Strait, Panay offers Iloilo's food scene and its January Dinagyang, mangoes on Guimaras, the hot-bath villages of Antique and Boracay at the island's northern tip. In the east, Leyte and Samar are less visited, with the San Juanico Bridge, the Kalanggaman sandbar, Biliran's waterfalls and the caves of Samar.

Most of these trips mix fast craft, roll-on roll-off ferries and long van rides, and sea travel stops whenever storm signals go up, which happens most often in the second half of the year. Book the boat leg with some slack, and check schedules and fares close to the date, since routes are added and dropped from one season to the next.

mindanao.title: Mindanao Travel Guides: Siargao, Camiguin and Davao
mindanao.description: Mindanao travel guides: Siargao, Camiguin, Davao and Mount Apo, Bukidnon, Cagayan de Oro rafting, Lake Sebu and the coves of Surigao, with planning notes.
mindanao.keywords: Mindanao travel guides, Siargao, Camiguin, Davao, Samal Island, Mount Apo, Cagayan de Oro, Bukidnon, Lake Sebu, Surigao, Bucas Grande, Tinuy-an Falls, Dapitan
intro: Mindanao is the large southern island group of the Philippines, split into six regions: Zamboanga Peninsula, Northern Mindanao, the Davao Region, SOCCSKSARGEN, Caraga and BARMM. Distances are long and road trips between regions can take most of a day, so most visitors fly into one city and stay in one area rather than trying to cover the whole island.

The northeast is where many first trips go. Siargao is the surf island, and the Siargao from Cebu guide compares the flight with the overnight boat route. Nearby in Surigao are the lagoons of Bucas Grande, the Enchanted River in Hinatuan and Tinuy-an Falls in Bislig. Off the northern coast, Camiguin is a compact volcanic island that fits a long weekend, and its Lanzones Festival fills Mambajao every October.

Inland and to the south, the trips change character. Cagayan de Oro is known for white-water rafting and Bukidnon for its cool highlands and adventure parks. Davao combines a big, easygoing city with Samal Island and the foothills of Mount Apo, the highest mountain in the Philippines, where the Philippine Eagle Center cares for the national bird. Farther south, Lake Sebu is home to T'boli communities and a string of waterfalls, while Dapitan in the west keeps the place where Jose Rizal lived in exile.

Safety conditions vary a lot from one province to another, and the destinations in these guides are established tourist areas. Before travelling overland into places you do not know, check current advisories and ask your accommodation or the local tourism office about the route. Flight schedules to smaller airports change often, so confirm them before you plan connections.
